session_note: The 2025 Wisconsin Legislature's biennial session period runs from noon on Monday, January 6, 2025, through noon on Monday, January 4, 2027 (per 2025 Senate Joint Resolution 1, which sets the session calendar). SJR 1 also schedules the floor periods within that biennium; for 2026 these are January 13-15/20-22, February 10-19, March 17-19 (expressly designated the last general-business floor period), April 14-16 (limited-business only), and May 12-13 (veto review only), with March 20, 2026 through January 4, 2027 designated as an interim period for committee work (and the 2027 inauguration). 'Failed to pass pursuant to Senate Joint Resolution 1' is Wisconsin's standard constructive-failure mechanism: SJR 1 provides that a bill which has not been acted on by both houses by the close of the applicable floor period is automatically deemed failed, with no separate vote required to kill it. Because all seven items below failed on 2026-03-23 - the Monday immediately after the March 17-19, 2026 period that SJR 1 itself labels the LAST general-business floor period - and because the only floor time remaining in the biennium (April 2026 limited-business and May 2026 veto-review) is procedurally restricted to narrow categories of business that would not encompass these general bills, this failure is, as a practical matter, final for the 2025-2026 biennium. The biennium does not formally end until January 4, 2027, and a bill could in theory still be revived via an extraordinary/special session called by petition of the legislature or the Governor, but no such session has been convened or scheduled for any of these measures as of the research date, so all are correctly treated as dead (failed_died) rather than carried_over.

It never received a committee hearing before failing at the SJR 1 deadline; it is dead for the 2025-2026 biennium under current legislative scheduling, though a special/extraordinary session could theoretically revive it before the biennium's formal close on 2027-01-04 (no such session has been convened for this bill).
